title: Boomerang: signed claim or permissionless refund
security_scope: Original WIP teaching policy, not ready for real funds. A funded instance curries one immutable tuple (recipient public key, recipient puzzle hash, refund puzzle hash, amount in mojos, absolute Unix deadline in seconds). Claim emits AGG_SIG_ME with a fixed 32-byte intent, a strictly-before deadline assertion, ASSERT_MY_AMOUNT, and the full recipient payout. Refund at or after the deadline emits the same amount assertion and full fixed refund payout with no signature. The template itself accepts configurable terms; only the actual curried reveal commits them. Exact bool/list/byte-width/canonical-u64 ABI checks apply on both paths, without positivity or future-time restrictions. VM vector acceptance means conditions were produced, not that a signature, timestamp, key curve validity or ledger spend was validated. Someone must submit the refund; any fee must come from another input. Finite differential and simulator checks are not compiler-preservation or security proofs.

provenance.source_origin: All three paired source files are original implementations of this explicit teaching contract. No published canonical module or module hash is claimed.
limitations: This is not CHIP-0044 clawback: that published entitlement schedule differs from recipient-before/refund-after. The pinned CHIP is a comparison reference, not source copied into this puzzle.

The recipient public key and payout hash are independent creator-selected commitments; the policy does not prove that the key controls that destination or that the refund destination belongs to a particular person.
The fixed claim intent is exactly the ASCII bytes chialisp-oxide/boomerang/claim:1; AGG_SIG_ME additionally binds the actual coin ID and the consensus network domain.
PublicKey is an exact 48-byte source/wire value, not a source-level curve-membership proof. Consensus verifies the actual claim signature separately.
Zero and maximum u64 amounts/deadlines are valid template inputs. Some choices yield unusable claim windows or unsuitable ledger policies; no additional hidden source restriction is imposed.
The remaining curried solution is exactly a one-element proper bool list: (1) claims and (()) refunds. No caller-supplied time, replacement terms, arbitrary message or fee choice is accepted.

Permissionless return requires a submitted transaction. No automatic refund process, fee reward, censorship resistance, formal Optional/signature/ledger model, or absence of all security breaches is claimed.
